**Verdict:** RECOMMENDED

### Practical Recommendation
Prioritize **Thursday, January 14 at Niseko United** for your primary session, and use **Wednesday, January 13 at Rusutsu** only if you want an extra day and are willing to buy a day ticket. 

* **The Missed Opportunity (Thursday Alpine Reopening):** While Wednesday boasts bigger snowfall totals (9″ opening + 3″ day), Niseko’s exposed upper lifts—already wind-held Tuesday—will almost certainly remain shuttered under 55 mph westerly gusts. Thursday offers the classic storm-recovery payoff: winds plummet to 22 mph, temperatures remain sub-freezing, and upper lifts/gates should reopen to reveal 13″+ of preserved storm snow across Niseko’s steep alpine bowls and off-piste gates. It is 100% covered on your Ikon Pass and requires zero highway driving.
* **Wednesday Tactical Pivot (Rusutsu):** If you choose to ski Wednesday, do not stay at Niseko to fight crowd bottlenecks on wind-sheltered lower groomers. Instead, take your rental car 35–45 minutes around Mt. Yotei to Rusutsu. Rusutsu sits under much lighter winds (28 mph gusts vs. Niseko’s 55 mph), and its heavily forested ridges on East Mountain and Mt. Isola protect lift operations and preserve 7–9″ of light powder. Because Rusutsu is an Epic partner, not Ikon, you will need to pay out of pocket for a single-day lift ticket (~¥11,500–¥14,500 / $75–$95), which easily fits your spend preference.

### Decision Triggers
* **Roads:** Check Hokkaido road closure reports for Route 66 and Route 276/230 early Wednesday morning. Heavy drifting around Makkari/Kimobetsu can close access to Rusutsu. If closed, take a rest day.
* **Morning Lift Reports:** If Niseko reports surprise lower-mountain wind holds or delays on Wednesday morning, Rusutsu is mandatory for turns. On Thursday at 08:00, monitor the Niseko United lift status; once the top quad chairs (e.g., King Hooded Quad #4 / Ace #4) and gates are slated to open, stage early for first tracks.
